newsitem.title: FRANCE: French MP sees Lagardere keeping TMM stake.
newsitem.headline: French MP sees Lagardere keeping TMM stake.

text.p: A member of parliament in France's ruling RPR coalition on Thursday raised the possibility of Lagardere retaining a stake in Thomson Multimedia after its planned sale to Daewoo Electronics.

"One could imagine, for example, that the Lagardere group stayed a partner in Thomson Multimedia with Daewoo," Patrick Devedjian told the newspaper La Tribune Desfosses. Devedjian has been asked to study setting up a parliamentary finance committee inquiry into the Thomson SA privatisation,
"This guarantee by the Lagardere group would be based on maintaining a stake in Thomson Multimedia..." he said.
Lagardere's holding in Thomson Multimedia (TMM) could be temporary and a minority stake, he said.
Devedjian said he thought there was a racism and condescension toward Daewoo which was unacceptable in the current political debate.

Daewoo had given commitments on safeguarding jobs but these were not taken seriously, so there were efforts to come up with credible guarantees, he said. It was in this context that he raised the possibility of Lagardere keeping a TMM stake.

The Thomson privatisation, particularly plans to sell loss-making TMM to Daewoo for a symbolic one franc, has aroused opposition not only among unions, the socialist and communist parties but in the ranks of the parliamentary majority.
Former prime minister Edouard Balladur and a member of the Gaullist RPR party told the VSD magazine in an interview released on Wednesday that he disapproved of the handling of the Thomson sale.

Prime Minister Alain Juppe last week unexpectedly announced that there would be a parliamentary debate, but no vote, on the Thomson sale after the Privatisation Commission gives its decision on the state's choice for the Lagardere bid.
Daewoo chairman Kim Woo-choong told the newspaper Le Figaro on Thursday the group would almost certainly set up its Daewoo European headquarters in Paris if its TMM bid were accepted.

Daewoo launched a massive French newspaper advertising campaign on Wednesday to support its bid in the face of growing public criticism to the deal. On Wednesday, some 1,500 people joined a march of Thomson Multimedia workers in Angers, west France, to protest against the sale.
Devedjian said there was an industrial logic in merging Lagardere's Matra with Thomson-CSF.
"The decision to create the world number two in the sector by merging Matra and Thomson-CSF is a coherent one," he said. -- Paris newsroom +33 1 4221 5452
